summary.short_summary: Imaginary Content, owned by Ilene Richardson, has transitioned to specializing in e-commerce after eight years as Craft’s Agency of Record (AOR), focusing on managing Product Detail Page (PDP) content for the US and Canada. The company collaborates with significant brands such as Tyson and Lactalis and is undertaking new projects like Jet Puffed candy content shooting. It has a fully equipped content studio established 2.5 years ago, featuring a kitchen and flexible configurations, conveniently located near NYC. The brand onboarding fee ranges from $5,000 to $10,000, with competitive monthly retainers starting at $20,000, making their services appealing compared to traditional 4A agencies. There are partnership opportunities for three-month projects focused on Amazon creative adaptations, and Common Good frequently requests high-volume social media content production, which Imaginary Content can fulfill due to its studio capabilities. Both agencies are adept at food styling, with Imaginary Content working with high-profile clients like Martha Stewart, and they prefer agency-to-agency partnerships for scalable projects. Common Good is currently pitching for a major category leader that requires a comprehensive content overhaul, which could present significant collaboration budget opportunities. Andy Day is facilitating strategic introductions as part of an $8-10 million EBITDA rollup strategy, positioning Common Good as a key partner.
